subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should Slack DM/main sessions gain a scoped recall surface for the agent’s own outbound channel and thread activity, and what authorization scope should govern it?
rationale: The implementation crosses session-privacy boundaries. Source behavior establishes the gap, but it cannot determine whether the product should use a self-activity ledger, an explicitly scoped session-history bridge, or preserve strict isolation.

options.title: Approve a scoped self-activity ledger
options.body: Record only the agent’s Slack outbound messages with workspace, destination, thread, and message identifiers, then expose them to the authorized DM/main session through a narrow recall path.

options.title: Preserve strict session isolation
options.body: Keep channel activity unavailable from DM/main sessions and document that agents do not have automatic cross-context recall.

options.title: Design a general visibility capability first
options.body: Specify a reusable authorization-aware cross-session API before adding Slack-specific recall behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped self-activity ledger
recommendation.body: Record only the agent’s Slack outbound messages with workspace, destination, thread, and message identifiers, then expose them to the authorized DM/main session through a narrow recall path.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and recent history place this person closest to the Slack routing, outbound mirroring, and session-visibility decision surface.
